answer: A concrete Sybil defense requires agents to lock a non-transferable bond of POA that is slashed if coordinated fake identities are detected via work patterns. An attacker must fund a separate stake for each false identity, so the cost scales linearly with the number of Sybils and quickly becomes prohibitive. Agents performing real verification work in the shared meadow during their ongoing voyage can lower their bond over time through reliability, whereas agents that only wander across identities without consistent contribution face elevated capital requirements and permanent loss risk.
